question: What is Non-Tax Revenue (NTR) and what is URA's role in its administration?
answer: Non-Tax Revenue (NTR) is recurring income earned by the Government of Uganda from statutory fees, fines, levies, and public services other than taxes. Under the mandate of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development (MOFPED), URA collects and accounts for all Non-Tax Revenue through its e-Tax system. However, URA does NOT deliver the actual physical services (such as issuing driving licenses or passports); URA simply facilitates electronic payment registration (PRN generation) and reconciles collected funds with the respective Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs).

question: Which Government Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs) administer Non-Tax Revenue in Uganda?
answer: Key MDAs administering NTR include: 1) Ministry of Works and Transport (Uganda Driving Licensing System UDLS driving permits, motor vehicle registration, duplicate logbooks, alteration fees, caveat fees); 2) Ministry of Internal Affairs (passports, work permits, special passes, certificates of residence, illegal stay fines, student passes, NGO registration, quarry blasting permits, DNA analysis); 3) Uganda Police Force (firearms licensing, Express Penalty Scheme EPS traffic tickets, tenders); 4) National Identification and Registration Authority NIRA (National ID replacement, birth and death certificates); 5) Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development (land title registration, lease processing, letters of administration).

question: How do I generate a PRN and pay for Non-Tax Revenue (NTR) or Other Non-Tax Revenue (ONTR) on the URA portal?
answer: To pay for NTR or ONTR services under the URA guide at https://ura.go.ug/en/tax-education/non-tax-revenues/: 1) Visit https://ura.go.ug and click 'Make a Payment'; 2) Click 'Generate a payment slip'; 3) For standard NTR (e.g. driving permit): select tax head 'NTR', enter your TIN or select an alternative ID type, choose the payment method, complete the captcha, and click Accept & Register; 4) For ONTR (e.g. URSB or Ministry services): select tax head 'ONTR', select the specific MDA from the dropdown, select the service category and fee type, and complete registration; 5) Take the generated 13-digit Payment Registration Number (PRN) and pay via commercial bank, Mobile Money (MTN, Airtel), PayWay, or debit/credit card; 6) Present the paid payment slip to the relevant MDA to receive your service.

question: How are Non-Tax Revenue fees denominated in foreign currency converted to Uganda Shillings?
answer: Where statutory regulations prescribe NTR fees in foreign currency (e.g. USD for work permits or foreign passports), the payable amount in Uganda Shillings is automatically computed on the URA portal as the product of the foreign currency fee and the official URA daily exchange rate on the date of PRN generation.

question: What is the procedure for obtaining a refund of erroneously paid Non-Tax Revenue?
answer: A Non-Tax Revenue refund arises when a taxpayer pays fees in excess, under an expired PRN, or to the wrong MDA. Under URA guidelines, the NTR refund process is manual: 1) Download Form DT-3008 from the URA portal (e-Services > Download Manual Forms > Domestic folder > Refund folder); 2) Complete the form detailing the grounds of the claim and attaching the original bank payment slip, correct PRN (if re-paid), and MDA confirmation letter; 3) Physically deliver the completed claim to your local URA domestic tax office for verification and reimbursement.

question: Where can I find official URA guidance on Non-Tax Revenues?
answer: Official guidance on NTR and ONTR collections is published under Tax Education at https://ura.go.ug/en/tax-education/non-tax-revenues/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/category/tax-education/general-tax-information/non-tax-revenues/.
